title: KCP events_read result (DESIGN.md §11.3, §11.4, §11.6.1 read family)
description: CommandResult.result payload for events_read (§11.2 ok arm; the envelope's revision/event_cursor members live outside this payload). §11.4 events_read result verbatim: { events[], next_cursor, snapshot_epoch }; result events are the §11.3 event envelope embedded per operation (gap note KG28). If a cursor predates available history the command instead fails with cursor-expired plus snapshot recovery data (§11.4).

events.description: Authorized §11.3 event envelopes; at most 512 (§11.8 page/event read limit).

snapshot_epoch.description: Opaque snapshot epoch for cursor-expired recovery (§11.4).

cursor.description: Opaque, authenticated cursor or snapshot token (§11.3, §11.5); the 4096-char ceiling is the K0 cursor-cap extraction decision (spec/schemas/README.md item 9).

digestHex.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 value of a §11.8 typed digest; the digest type/domain is fixed by the schema field holding it (§11.8: a bare 32-byte value cannot be substituted across digest fields).

payload.description: Inline event payload validated by the schema at schema_ref; registered application event payloads are capped at 64 KiB (§11.8), enforced at admission. Any JSON value here; each payload schema closes it.

payload_ref.description: Durable reference to an externalized payload; access is authorized at read time (§11.4).

eventEnvelope.description: Event envelope per §11.3, field-for-field, with the payload | payload_ref alternation (mirrors kcp-command-suite kcp-event.schema.json; ops schemas are self-contained, so the shape is embedded here — gap note KG28).

eventType.description: Reverse-domain event type name ending in a major version, e.g. dev.kovee.space.contribution-appended.v1 (§11.3). A breaking payload change uses a new major event type (§11.9). Major versions start at 1 (the § shows only .v1 and never a .v0) — recorded extraction decision.

ext.description: Extensions keyed by a reverse-domain namespace (§11.9); never interpreted as identity, authorization, budget, or policy.

identifier.description: Opaque identifier, at most 128 bytes (§11.8); visible-ASCII alphabet is a K0 extraction decision (spec/schemas/README.md).

safeNonNegativeInteger.description: I-JSON safe integer (§11.8 rejects unsafe integers).

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 date-time (recorded K0 extraction decision, spec/schemas/README.md item 7); format: date-time additionally requires semantic calendar validity (R0 KENV-05).
